binary-trees.c: One malloc and one free per node through the C library.
binary-trees.miri: One reference-counted allocation per node from the runtime's block cache, close to Rust in time; each node carries a reference-count header C does not, so peak memory is higher.
binary-trees.rust: One Box allocation and one drop per node on the system allocator, close to C.

fannkuch-redux.c: Integer loops over a small array, unchecked.
fannkuch-redux.miri: Every array access keeps a bounds check the optimiser cannot hoist because the loop bound is a parameter, and the counters are overflow-checked.
fannkuch-redux.rust: The same loops with bounds checks the optimiser mostly removes.

mandelbrot.c: A scalar floating-point loop with no allocation.
mandelbrot.miri: At parity: the same scalar loop with no allocation.
mandelbrot.rust: The same scalar loop as C.

matmul.c: A strict floating-point inner product over row pointers, with unchecked reads.
matmul.miri: A bounds check per read like Rust, plus the inner row's header reloaded on every read and a check the optimiser cannot hoist because the bound is a parameter.
matmul.rust: The same loop with a bounds check on every read; measured, this is Rust's whole distance from C here, since Rust with unchecked indexing runs at C's speed and C gains nothing from its vectorisers.

nbody.c: Straight-line floating-point code over an array of structs; clang's straight-line vectoriser contributes part of its speed (measured by turning it off).
nbody.miri: Close to C: the remaining distance is a reference-count increment and decrement per step and floating-point values spilled around calls.
nbody.rust: The same code with bounds checks the optimiser removes.

sieve.c: One flag per byte, written with unchecked strided stores.
sieve.miri: A bounds check on every strided write, like Rust; memory matches C.
sieve.rust: The same flags with a bounds check on every strided write.

spectral-norm.c: A serial floating-point reduction; clang's vectorisers add nothing here (measured by turning them off).
spectral-norm.miri: Not yet explained at the current size: vectorisation is ruled out, and whether a call or a spill remains in the inner loop has still to be read from the disassembly.
spectral-norm.rust: The same reduction with bounds checks.

wordfreq.c: Counts with the suite's shared chained hash table (see the port notes), keyed by views into the input.
wordfreq.miri: Reads lines lazily and holds the input once, but every word is an owned string, hashed through the generic identity path, and every update probes the map twice.
wordfreq.rust: A HashMap keyed by borrowed slices, hashed with SipHash.

fannkuch-redux: At size S the cold time is mostly process start-up ; read the hot time for this workload at size S.
C and C++ index without bounds checks by language; Miri, Rust, Go, Python and TypeScript check every index, and the ratio includes that cost (charter section 4).
matmul: C's lead over Rust here is bounds checking, not vectorisation: on x86-64 the C port runs as fast with clang's vectorisers off, and the Rust port with unchecked indexing runs at C's speed. C and C++ index without bounds checks by language; Miri, Rust, Go, Python and TypeScript check every index, and the ratio includes that cost (charter section 4).
sieve: C and C++ index without bounds checks by language; Miri, Rust, Go, Python and TypeScript check every index, and the ratio includes that cost (charter section 4).
spectral-norm: C's lead over Rust here is not vectorisation: on x86-64 the C port runs as fast with clang's vectorisers off. C and C++ index without bounds checks by language; Miri, Rust, Go, Python and TypeScript check every index, and the ratio includes that cost (charter section 4).
wordfreq: The C port counts with the suite's shared chained hash table (bench/c/table.h), hashed with FNV-1a, the cheapest hash on the chart; every other port uses its standard map and that map's hash (Rust's is SipHash, slower per key and resistant to collision attacks).
